exercises.title: How many calls does naive fib(n) make? Solve the recurrence, do not run it
exercises.problemHtml:
The naive fib(n) (if n < 2 return n, else fib(n−1) + fib(n−2)) makes C(n) calls in total, where C(0) = C(1) = 1 and C(n) = C(n−1) + C(n−2) + 1. Complete:

  • static long calls(int n) — C(n) for 0 ≤ n ≤ 85, computed from the recurrence bottom-up (a loop or a memo), not by calling fib;
  • static long callsOf(int n, int k) — how many times fib(k) itself is called while computing fib(n) (0 ≤ k ≤ n): 1 for k = n; for k < n it follows a Fibonacci pattern (work it out on the recursion tree of fib(5)).

⏱ Complexity check. One case runs your code on a large input (n = 85) inside a 2-second limit. An O(n) solution finishes in a fraction of a second on any ordinary laptop; an running the exponential recursion and counting one needs far longer and the case prints TOO SLOW. C(85) is about 4·10¹⁷ calls. The limit is generous on purpose — if it fails, the algorithm is the problem, not your machine.

Run the grader on your machine

The website does NOT grade this exercise. Press Tải .zip (download) above the code, unzip it, edit the code in src/, then inside the exercise folder (the one with cham.mjs) run:

node cham.mjs

The zip unpacks into a folder named after the exercise (<folder> below). Windows (PowerShell): cd "$env:USERPROFILE\Downloads\<folder>" — cmd: cd /d %USERPROFILE%\Downloads\<folder> — then node cham.mjs. macOS (Terminal): cd ~/Downloads/<folder> then node cham.mjs. Tip: type cd and drag the folder into the terminal window. You need Node.js 18+ and JDK 8 or newer (17 or 21 recommended) — javac -version must work.

The grader compiles src/ with javac, runs 2 case(s) (1 hidden — not printed in this text), compares your output line by line (trailing spaces and Windows/macOS line endings ignored), prints a diff of the wrong lines and gives a score. When it prints ALL CHECKS PASSED, come back and press Tự đánh dấu đã giải (self-mark as solved). node cham.mjs --case 2 --show prints the input and your whole output for case 2.

Requirements

  • No call to a real fib — O(n) arithmetic.
  • Values up to n = 85 fit in a long.
exercises.problemHtmlVi:
Hàm fib(n) ngây thơ (n < 2 trả n, ngược lại fib(n−1) + fib(n−2)) gọi tổng cộng C(n) lần, với C(0) = C(1) = 1 và C(n) = C(n−1) + C(n−2) + 1. Hoàn thiện calls(n) — C(n) với 0 ≤ n ≤ 85, tính từ dưới lên theo hệ thức (vòng lặp hoặc bảng nhớ), không gọi fib; và callsOf(n, k) — trong lúc tính fib(n) thì chính fib(k) được gọi bao nhiêu lần (0 ≤ k ≤ n): k = n là 1; k < n theo một quy luật Fibonacci (vẽ cây đệ quy của fib(5) để tìm).

⏱ Kiểm độ phức tạp. Một ca chạy code của bạn với input LỚN (n = 85) trong hạn 2 giây. Lời giải O(n) xong trong chưa tới một giây trên laptop bình thường; bản running the exponential recursion and counting cần lâu hơn rất nhiều và ca in TOO SLOW. C(85) khoảng 4·10¹⁷ lời gọi. Hạn đặt rộng có chủ ý — trượt ca này thì do thuật toán, không phải do máy bạn.

Windows (PowerShell): cd "$env:USERPROFILE\Downloads\<thư-mục>" — cmd: cd /d %USERPROFILE%\Downloads\<thư-mục> — rồi node cham.mjs. macOS (Terminal): cd ~/Downloads/<thư-mục> rồi node cham.mjs. Mẹo: gõ cd rồi kéo thư mục vào cửa sổ terminal. Cần Node.js 18+ và JDK 8 trở lên (khuyên 17 hoặc 21) — javac -version phải chạy được.

exercises.solutionExplanationHtml: The recurrence C(n) = C(n−1) + C(n−2) + 1 has the solution C(n) = 2F(n+1) − 1, so naive fib makes Θ(φⁿ) calls — the recursion tree analysis of the lesson. fib(k) for k ≥ 1 appears F(n−k+1) times and fib(0) as often as fib(2): the waste memoization removes.
exercises.solutionExplanationHtmlVi: Hệ thức C(n) = C(n−1) + C(n−2) + 1 có nghiệm C(n) = 2F(n+1) − 1, nên fib ngây thơ gọi Θ(φⁿ) lần — đúng phép phân tích cây đệ quy của bài. fib(k) với k ≥ 1 xuất hiện F(n−k+1) lần và fib(0) nhiều như fib(2): sự lãng phí mà ghi nhớ loại bỏ.

mistakesJson.loi: Answering by actually running the naive recursion with a counter — C(85) ≈ 4·10¹⁷ calls never finish.|||Trả lời bằng cách chạy thật đệ quy ngây thơ có bộ đếm — C(85) ≈ 4·10¹⁷ lời gọi không bao giờ xong.
Forgetting the "+ 1" of the call itself — that gives F(n+1) instead of C(n) = 2F(n+1) − 1.|||Quên "+ 1" của chính lời gọi đó — ra F(n+1) thay vì C(n) = 2F(n+1) − 1.

exercises.title: Count inversions in O(n log n) — merge sort with a counter
exercises.problemHtml:
An inversion is a pair i < j with a[i] > a[j]. Complete static long inversions(int[] a) (a may be changed — sort it on the way). Checking every pair is O(n²); instead sort with merge sort and count during the merge: when an element of the right half is taken before the remaining elements of the left half, it forms an inversion with each of them.

[2,4,1,3,5] → 3 ((2,1), (4,1), (4,3)). The master theorem gives T(n) = 2T(n/2) + O(n) = O(n log n).

⏱ Complexity check. One case runs your code on a large input (n = 1,000,000) inside a 3-second limit. An O(n log n) solution finishes in a fraction of a second on any ordinary laptop; an O(n²) one needs far longer and the case prints TOO SLOW. Checking all pairs of a million values is 5·10¹¹ comparisons. The limit is generous on purpose — if it fails, the algorithm is the problem, not your machine.

Run the grader on your machine

The website does NOT grade this exercise. Press Tải .zip (download) above the code, unzip it, edit the code in src/, then inside the exercise folder (the one with cham.mjs) run:

node cham.mjs

The zip unpacks into a folder named after the exercise (<folder> below). Windows (PowerShell): cd "$env:USERPROFILE\Downloads\<folder>" — cmd: cd /d %USERPROFILE%\Downloads\<folder> — then node cham.mjs. macOS (Terminal): cd ~/Downloads/<folder> then node cham.mjs. Tip: type cd and drag the folder into the terminal window. You need Node.js 18+ and JDK 8 or newer (17 or 21 recommended) — javac -version must work.

The grader compiles src/ with javac, runs 3 case(s) (2 hidden — not printed in this text), compares your output line by line (trailing spaces and Windows/macOS line endings ignored), prints a diff of the wrong lines and gives a score. When it prints ALL CHECKS PASSED, come back and press Tự đánh dấu đã giải (self-mark as solved). node cham.mjs --case 2 --show prints the input and your whole output for case 2.

Requirements

  • O(n log n).
  • Equal values are not inversions.

exercises.title: Maximum subarray by divide and conquer (best crossing the middle)
exercises.problemHtml:
Complete static long maxSub(int[] a, int lo, int hi): the largest sum of a non-empty contiguous part of a[lo..hi]. Divide at mid; the answer is the best of: the left half, the right half, and the best part crossing mid (the best suffix of the left half ending at mid + the best prefix of the right half starting at mid + 1, each found with one loop).

[-2,1,-3,4,-1,2,1,-5,4] → 6 (4,-1,2,1); all negative → the largest single element.

⏱ Complexity check. One case runs your code on a large input (n = 1,000,000) inside a 3-second limit. An O(n log n) solution finishes in a fraction of a second on any ordinary laptop; an O(n²) (every start, every end) one needs far longer and the case prints TOO SLOW. The limit is generous on purpose — if it fails, the algorithm is the problem, not your machine.

The website does NOT grade this exercise. Press Tải .zip (download) above the code, unzip it, edit the code in src/, then inside the exercise folder (the one with cham.mjs) run:

node cham.mjs

The zip unpacks into a folder named after the exercise (<folder> below). Windows (PowerShell): cd "$env:USERPROFILE\Downloads\<folder>" — cmd: cd /d %USERPROFILE%\Downloads\<folder> — then node cham.mjs. macOS (Terminal): cd ~/Downloads/<folder> then node cham.mjs. Tip: type cd and drag the folder into the terminal window. You need Node.js 18+ and JDK 8 or newer (17 or 21 recommended) — javac -version must work.

The grader compiles src/ with javac, runs 3 case(s) (2 hidden — not printed in this text), compares your output line by line (trailing spaces and Windows/macOS line endings ignored), prints a diff of the wrong lines, checks the source rules and gives a score. When it prints ALL CHECKS PASSED, come back and press Tự đánh dấu đã giải (self-mark as solved). node cham.mjs --case 2 --show prints the input and your whole output for case 2.

Requirements

  • Recursive divide and conquer: O(n log n).
  • Non-empty part; sums in long.

exercises.solutionExplanationHtml: Two half-size subproblems plus a linear crossing scan: T(n) = 2T(n/2) + Θ(n) = Θ(n log n), and the recursion depth is only log₂ n. (Kadane’s algorithm does it in O(n) — the ⭐ CS.2 lesson — but this is the textbook divide-and-conquer example of the master theorem.)
exercises.solutionExplanationHtmlVi: Hai bài toán con cỡ một nửa cộng một lượt quét tuyến tính cắt qua giữa: T(n) = 2T(n/2) + Θ(n) = Θ(n log n), và độ sâu đệ quy chỉ log₂ n. (Thuật toán Kadane làm trong O(n) — bài ⭐ CS.2 — nhưng đây là ví dụ chia để trị chuẩn của định lý thợ.)

mistakesJson.loi: Starting the crossing sums at 0 — for all-negative input the crossing part becomes empty and the answer 0.|||Khởi tạo tổng cắt qua bằng 0 — với dữ liệu toàn âm, đoạn cắt qua thành rỗng và đáp án là 0.
Trying every (start, end) pair — O(n²), the complexity check fails.|||Thử mọi cặp (đầu, cuối) — O(n²), trượt kiểm độ phức tạp.
